cool! well since we are on the discussion of collisions can i give u another one that happens to fix. this one i think is probably easier to find out, but it requires a real change;

so, if i place a floor, then a wall, and then either a floor or a roof above it, and then go to the area, and then jump, my head collides with the piece above, and then causes the player model to do a bunch of glitchy movement,
resolution: Fixed the head-into-ceiling glitch and shaped it to the user's CSS-bhop feel. Jumping under a floor/roof/deck placed overhead made the player's head poke into the piece's solid band; the physics step had no vertical (head-bonk) response, so collideSolidRects treated the overlap as a horizontal intrusion and side-pushed the player around (the glitchy jitter). A ceiling is a surface whose normal points down, so the correct response removes only the velocity component INTO it (the upward part) and keeps horizontal momentum. Added ceilingUndersideAt() (framework/game/physics.zig) which finds the lowest solid-rect underside, finite-floor band only — walls have none, with the body column inside the footprint, axis-aligned and oriented rects alike; step() clamps the head just below it and zeroes rising velocity BEFORE collideSolidRects so the band overlap is gone and the horizontal push never fires on a ceiling. pvx/pvz are deliberately preserved per the user's request — you skim a low hallway at full speed (Source-style head-skim, bhop-feel) instead of being shoved to a stop. Added deterministic test 'head bonk: jumping into a ceiling caps the head and keeps horizontal speed' asserting the head never punches through, rising velocity zeroed at contact, and +x speed survives. no-V8 world_loader builds clean; game-physics 40/41 (the one red, hollow-ramp-slab rect step-up surface_speed, predates this work). SHA aee4d158a. Needs Compile + relaunch (loader Zig change).
